newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Becton Dickinson to boost Asia investments.
newsitem.headline: Becton Dickinson to boost Asia investments.

text.p: Becton Dickinson, a U.S.-based medical devices and diagnostic products maker, plans to raise investments in India and China by more than US$100 million over five years, its president for Asia Pacific said on Thursday.
Eugenio Naschold said the company also plans to expand more aggressively in sales and marketing in South Korea as well as introduce more product lines.
"Because of the aggressive investments, we expect to double our sales (In the region) every three years or so," Naschold told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"Definitely we expect much better profitability and we now have a higher order of sales."

With worries about AIDS growing in Asia, the company's strategy is to convert and educate the public to switch to disposable medical devices. "We create the market rather than compete for market share with our competitors," he said.
Becton Dickinson already has a $6 million investment at Bawal, in India's Haryana state, which will start production in September.
Two weeks ago, Becton's board gave it approval for an additional $40 million investment. Work on the plant will start in April with production scheduled to begin 18 months after that.

The Indian facility will produce intravenous and hypodermic syringes. "We forsee in the next five years we will be investing a total of $100 million in India, including the existing investments," Naschold said.
By taking advantage of the low manufacturing costs in India, Becton plans to sell its products not only in India but also to other countries in the Indian subcontinent and the Middle East, he said.

Becton also plans to boost its investments in China to between $80 million and $100 million in five years from the current $40 million. It now has a plant at the China-Singapore Suzhou Industrial Park, a city within a city in Jiangsu Province.

Becton Dickinson operates in more than 80 countries. Among the products it makes are drug delivery and infusion systems, diabetes care and vaccination devices, surgical devices, microbiology and blood collection products.
